title: Open /skills directly as a searchable checklist
objective: Make exact /skills immediately open a keyboard-first searchable checklist whose rows show configured visibility, whose details distinguish current activation, and whose Space shortcut toggles the selected skill through the authoritative management backend.
context: Exact /skills has no intermediate action menu: it immediately loads the current catalog and shows checkbox rows. /skills list remains an explicit text subcommand, not an interactive menu entry.
Interactive toggles are project-local persistent overrides with immediate current-session effect.
The worktree is shared and dirty; only owned_files may be modified.

source_evidence.note: Bounded metadata catalog and progressive disclosure inspiration.
Live discovery and skill visibility controls.
Management must mutate live state without rewriting the existing prompt prefix.

include: Open the searchable skill checklist directly for exact /skills, start one authoritative Snapshot read immediately, and display status, name, summary, source, path, visibility, mutability, and effective scope.
Render a checkbox at the left of every row: auto, name-only, and manual-only are [x], while off is [ ]; fresh skills without an override therefore start selected without resetting persisted state.
Distinguish configured visibility from runtime activation: a non-off shadowed row remains [x], while selected details localize that it is currently inactive and name the winner stable ID.
Keep /skills list/show/set and other subcommands on the existing text command path; do not expose List Skills or Enable/Disable Skills as an intermediate menu.

Use Space to submit the selected row's stable SkillID and observed catalog revision, toggling between off and the backend-persisted last non-off visibility; restore auto when no prior non-off value exists.
Persist interactive changes as project-local overrides and apply them immediately to the current session through the one-call task_15 backend rather than direct filesystem or registry access.
Reject stale rows and active session overrides, refresh from the returned authoritative snapshot, and show how to clear a session override through the text command.
Keep managed read-only skills visible with a reason, but do not allow Space to mutate them.
Never optimistically commit a row: render committed/rejected/degraded results from the backend; when rollback fails, redraw from a fresh authoritative snapshot and show refresh-required state.

Support filter input, selection movement, inert Enter, Space-only mutation, one-Esc close, Backspace filter editing, empty states, loading states, and narrow terminal widths using existing TUI picker conventions.
Put every new user-visible menu, status, help, and error string behind semantic i18n keys with translations for all supported languages.
exclude: Do not modify command, registry, override-store, tool, or unrelated repl_tui.go production paths owned by other tasks.
Do not reduce the four-state backend to a boolean model.
Do not add dependencies or introduce a second modal framework.

implementation_steps: Define one direct checklist state plus pure filtering, selection, and visibility-toggle helpers; remove the obsolete primary-action state.
Wire the overlay into tui/app.go, tui/state.go, and tui/root.go through the launcher contract created by task_24.
Handle Space by invoking the shared backend once with stable ID and observed revision and redrawing from its committed, rejected, or degraded authoritative result.
Render state, scope, source/path details, read-only reasons, help text, and errors without exposing internal developer catalog messages.
Add focused tests for direct open/close behavior, checkbox rendering, keyboard filtering, last-state restoration, read-only rows, and backend failure rollback.
acceptance_criteria: Exact /skills immediately opens the searchable checklist and starts exactly one authoritative catalog read; no action menu or second Enter is required, while /skills subcommands still use text command routing.
Every row has a left checkbox: configured auto, name-only, and manual-only states render [x], and off renders [ ]; opening the list never resets a persisted off state.
A shadowed auto row renders [x] and a localized inactive-by-winner detail; toggling it off and on changes only its stable ID, and removing the winner removes the notice and restores active execution.
Space affects only the selected stable SkillID when its observed revision is current, and the authoritative updated state is visible without restarting the session.
Toggling name-only or manual-only off and back on restores that state instead of silently changing it to auto.
Last non-off restoration still works after closing/reopening the menu and after state reload; a skill with no remembered value returns to auto.
Managed read-only rows remain inspectable and Space reports why they cannot be changed.
Active session overrides and stale revisions reject the shortcut without mutating another scope or row.
Persistence or live-apply failures do not leave optimistic UI state behind; rollback failure is displayed as degraded and triggers authoritative refresh.
Enter never toggles a skill, Backspace only edits the filter, and one Esc closes the skills surface.
The interface remains usable with an empty catalog, an active filter, and a narrow terminal.
All new user-visible copy uses semantic i18n keys and the active runtime language.
risks: tui/app.go and tui/state.go remain task 30 integration points. tui/root.go is retained as task 30 delivery evidence, but final ownership transfers exclusively to task 31 for the isolated layout follow-up; preserve unrelated dirty changes and keep state isolated behind the task_24 launcher contract.
A naive UI-local boolean toggle would erase name-only/manual-only intent after reopen or restart; task_07/task_13 own durable restoration and transaction semantics.
Persistence may succeed while live apply fails unless the backend exposes one authoritative operation; do not compose two independent mutations inside the view.
non_goals: No session-only or arbitrary four-state editing in the Space shortcut; those remain text-command capabilities.
dispatch_prompt: Implement a direct /skills checklist with no intermediate action menu. Exact /skills immediately loads the authoritative snapshot; each row shows [x] unless effectively off, and Space alone sends stable SkillID plus observed revision to the one-call backend and redraws from committed/rejected/degraded results. Preserve text subcommand routing, last-non-off, session/read-only conflicts, and picker conventions. Modify only owned_files.
notes_for_assignee: Do not bypass task_15/task_24 interfaces or write settings directly. Remove the obsolete ListSkills launcher callback, but leave /skills list and all other explicit text subcommands on the normal command path.
follow_up_note: Task 30 remains the accepted interaction baseline. Task 31 separately owns terminal-cell single-line rendering, selected-only detail layout, resize behavior, and complete bordered-panel height containment.
